target_moa.text: Topical combination sunscreen (ecamsule 2%, avobenzone 2%, octocrylene 10%) that protects against UV radiation by absorption, scattering and reflection of incident UVR; ecamsule and avobenzone act as UVA filters and octocrylene acts mainly as a UVB filter, providing protection across the UVA and UVB spectrum

citations.quote:
Active ingredients: Active ingredients: ecamsule* 2%,
avobenzone 2%, octocrylene 10%.

The mechanism of action of all ______ lotions is believed to be ultraviolet radiation (UVR) protection by means of absorption, scattering and reflection of incident UVR, thereby reducing the direct penetration and effect of UVR.
Ecamsule (Trade name outside the USA is Mexoryl® SX) acts as a UVA filter. It has an absorption band from about 290-380 nm with the maximum absorbance at 344 nm. It is a new molecular entity.
Octocrylene acts mainly as a UVB filter. It has an absorption band from about 250-370 nm with the maximum absorbance at 303 nm.

modality.text: small molecule (topical combination sunscreen of three small-molecule UV filters; ecamsule is a new molecular entity)

Ecamsule is a new molecular entity in the United States.

key_safety.text: Acceptable OTC safety profile; most frequently reported adverse events were local application skin reactions (erythema, dermatitis, pruritus, edema, dry skin, skin irritation) or signs of eye irritation, with incidences not significantly different in children versus adults. In supportive studies there were 7 (2.1%) events of erythema/edema and 4 (1.2%) of papules considered treatment-related.

summary.text: NDA 21-502 was submitted May 12, 2005 as a 505(b)(2) application for Anthelios SX, a topical OTC combination sunscreen containing the new molecular entity ecamsule plus avobenzone and octocrylene. The FDA issued an approvable letter on March 10, 2006 for labeling deficiencies and trade-name concerns; the sponsor's May 18, 2006 complete response resolved these and the NDA was approved on July 21, 2006, with a deferred PREA pediatric study required for patients under 6 months of age.
